original_test_intent: Verify that a specifically approved reversible Socket Security Configuration policy persists across reboot and returns to the exact project default without weakening Secure Boot, TPM, measured boot, key databases, attestation, confidential-computing or hardware-protection state.
original_method: Inventory BIOS/TPM/security firmware, Secure Boot mode and PK/KEK/db/dbx identifiers, TPM ownership/provisioning/PCR policy, measured-boot/attestation and applicable security features; preserve logs; exclude irreversible or credential/key/fuse/TPM-clear actions; through KVM change one security-owner-approved reversible control, save/reboot and verify retained menu plus effective OS/attestation state; apply approved Load Defaults and confirm exact policy/key/protection restoration; stop on any unexpected trust-state delta or boot rejection and invoke only security-owner recovery.
manual_activity: A qualified BIOS operator and security owner jointly control the KVM workflow, approve the exact reversible policy, capture trust-state evidence and retain secure recovery material outside the DUT.
required_inputs: Platform/BIOS/TPM/security-firmware identity and exact Security Configuration page semantics
Project default matrix and one explicitly reversible test value with effective-state oracle
Secure Boot/key-database, TPM/PCR/provisioning, measured-boot/attestation and protection baseline
Maintenance, credentials/key custody, KVM/physical recovery and security incident/escalation plan
safety_requirements: Do not use all/random settings; exclude TPM clear, ownership/provisioning, key enrollment/deletion, fuse/one-time controls and credential changes
Never disable a protection unless the security owner explicitly defines bounded purpose, isolation and restored verification
Preserve TPM/event/boot/SEL/system evidence; no log or PCR manipulation to create a baseline
Verify effective trust state and boot chain after each save; menu persistence alone is insufficient
Stop on key/PCR/attestation/protection drift, recovery prompt, boot rejection or lost console; no automatic retry/CMOS clear
agent_execution_scope: Validate setting semantics, reversibility, default/test value, trust baseline, maintenance and owner-controlled recovery
Guide manual screenshots and collect effective Secure Boot/TPM/measured-boot/attestation/protection evidence before, retained and restored phases
Compare identifiers and state without exposing secrets or issuing the DUT verdict
Do not choose/change settings, handle private keys/secrets, clear TPM/logs, disable protections, reset firmware or invoke recovery
engineer_actions: Approve the one reversible security control and exact default/effective-state matrix; explicitly prohibit irreversible choices
Approve trust-state evidence, reboot/error criteria, Load-Defaults security effect and secure recovery/key custody
Review BIOS plus effective security evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: No SSH-only command can drive or visually validate BIOS security setup. Read-only OS/TPM/attestation commands are supporting evidence after the security-owner-controlled KVM actions.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Operator changes only the approved reversible control through KVM; collect menu screenshots and read-only effective trust-state evidence at baseline, retained and restored phases.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Security Configuration persistence/default cycle and 5/20-minute allocation remain; `all/random` does not authorize arbitrary or irreversible security changes.

modernized_recommendation.status: HIGH MANUAL SECURITY-POLICY PERSISTENCE AND TRUST-STATE RESTORATION TEST
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Test one approved reversible policy and prove both menu persistence and effective Secure Boot/TPM/measured-boot/attestation state, then verify exact secure restoration.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds irreversibility screening, security-owner control, key/TPM/attestation baseline, secret-safe evidence and incident recovery.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A menu can show the expected value while key databases, TPM policy or measured-boot state changed; Load Defaults may also reset policy without restoring project keys or protections.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Random security settings can cause data/secret loss, invalidate attestation, weaken protections, trigger recovery or make the system unbootable.

project_override_considerations: Factory Load Defaults may not equal the project's provisioned secure state and must never be assumed to restore PK/KEK/db/dbx, TPM ownership or attestation policy. Restoration requires an approved project-specific oracle and custody process.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, approval and platform/BIOS/TPM/security-firmware identity
Security-owner-approved reversible control, default/test/effective-state oracle and explicit prohibition list
Baseline, changed, retained, Load-Defaults and restored BIOS screenshots
Secure Boot mode and non-secret key identifiers, TPM/provisioning/PCR-policy status, measured-boot/attestation/protection comparison
Preserved event/TPM/SEL/boot/system evidence with secrets redacted and no unexplained delta

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2180 Wistron-BIOS-00497-V004: approve platform/BIOS/TPM/security identity, exact Security Configuration defaults and one safe reversible non-secret/non-provisioning value replacing `all/random`; define Secure Boot key-ID, TPM/PCR/provisioning, measured-boot/attestation/protection effective-state oracle, prohibited irreversible actions, Load-Defaults project impact, log preservation, aborts, key custody, and security-owner KVM/physical recovery.

review_improvement: Prevents a generic BIOS-default test from mutating the platform trust root and requires effective security restoration rather than relying on menu text or factory defaults.
independent_technical_reasoning: Security Configuration differs fundamentally from ordinary setup pages because some actions are irreversible or affect keys, TPM state and attestation. A random matrix is unacceptable. Even a reversible menu toggle must be checked at the effective trust layer, and Load Defaults cannot be presumed to reinstall project-specific keys or provisioning. The only safe review is manual, security-owner-gated, limited to one understood reversible control, with non-secret trust-state evidence and a separate recovery/custody plan.
